title: Revenue Recognition, Billing, Contracts, and Procurement Policy
author: Avery Thompson
content:
Purpose:
This document establishes Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies for budgeting & forecasting, contracts and legal approval flows, procurement procedures, and revenue recognition & billing. It aligns our practices with ASC 606 principles and ensures consistent financial treatment across Hosted API, Dedicated, Private deployments, and add-on services.

Scope:
Applies to all commercial contracts (customer and vendor), procurement requests, billing activities, and revenue recognition for Redwood Inference entities. Covers: hosted usage billing (per-token/embedding), reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual commits), private deployment licences, professional services, and add-ons (observability retention, compliance packages).

Key contacts and ownership:
- Finance owner: Avery Thompson (Head of Revenue Operations) — primary owner for revrec and billing policy
- Legal owner: Marcus Lee (Senior Counsel) — contract/legal process owner
- Procurement lead: Lina Patel (Procurement Manager) — vendor onboarding & PO approvals
- Billing ops: Sofia Ramirez (Billing Manager) — invoicing, collections, dunning

Relevant references:
- Related pages: /confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/finance-legal-budget-and-procurement-policy-2026 (Budget & procurement master policy)
- Accounting guidance: ASC 606 summary (internal link)
- Billing system: Stripe + internal billing microservice (api-billing)

1) Budgeting & Forecasting (Executive summary)
- Purpose: Produce a rolling 12-month forecast and annual budget that ties to booking-level assumptions, churn, average revenue per customer (ARPC), and product usage distribution (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private).
- Cadence and owners:
  - Monthly rolling forecast: Finance (FP&A) maintains a 12-month rolling forecast; updated by the 10th business day each month.
  - Annual budget: Prepared by Finance in collaboration with Product, Sales, and Engineering; board review in Q4 for the following year.
- Inputs and assumptions:
  - Bookings (new ARR/commits), churn (by cohort), upsell/expansion estimates, average contract term, price list changes, and model mix (open models vs. Redwood-verified).
  - Forecast sensitivity scenarios: base, upside (+15%), downside (-15%).
- Deliverables and metrics:
  - Monthly revenue forecast by revenue stream (usage-hosted, reserved-dedicated, private-licenses, professional services).
  - Cash forecast (90-day) maintained daily by Treasury for runway and cash management.
  - Key KPIs: MRR/ARR, Net Revenue Retention (NRR), Gross Margin %, Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) 

2) Contracts & Legal Approval Flow
- Contract types in scope:
  - Standard hosted API T&Cs (self-serve/online)
  - Customer master services agreements (MSA) and Statements of Work (SOW) for Dedicated/Private
  - Reseller/Marketplace agreements and vendor contracts
- Signature authority thresholds:
  - Up to $250k total contract value (TCV): Sales Director (with Legal review if non-standard terms).
  - $250k — $1M TCV: VP Sales + Legal signoff required.
  - > $1M TCV or deviations on security/compliance terms (e.g., SOC/attestations, on-prem requirements): CFO + Legal executive approval.
- Standard clauses and required exhibits:
  - Deliverables and performance obligations (explicitly enumerate hosting, reserved capacity, support SLAs).
  - Pricing schedule (unit metrics: per-token, per-embedding, per-reserved-GPU-hour), billing cadence, and payment terms.
  - Data residency and security attachments for Private deployments (KMS/HSM, audit logging).
  - Termination, refunds/credits, and dispute resolution language tied to service-level objective (SLO) metrics.
- Contract lifecycle steps (numbered procedure):
  1. Sales prepares redline from standard template in CLM system (DocuSign/CLM).
  2. Legal performs review and approves redlines within 3 business days (escalate to Counsel for novel risk).
  3. Finance validates pricing, billing rules, revenue account mapping, and payment terms.
  4. Approvals per signature authority.
  5. Counterparty signature and contract ingestion into CLM (assign contract ID and granularity of obligations).

3) Procurement Procedures (vendor and purchase process)
- Approved vendor onboarding:
  - All vendors > $5k annual expected spend must be run through procurement intake: vendor questionnaire, security review (if handling customer data), and tax/contracting checklist.
- Purchase request and PO flow:
  1. Requester raises purchase request in procurement system (NetSuite/ProcureNow) with cost center and GL code.
  2. Procurement reviews vendor terms and pricing (3 business days target).
  3. Approvals: Manager -> Finance BU owner -> Procurement lead (threshold-specific approvers for capital/one-time spend).
  4. PO issued and copy kept in procurement library; invoices only processed if matched to PO unless otherwise approved.
- Payment terms and vendor categorization:
  - Standard vendor payment terms: Net 30. Longer terms require Procurement + Treasury approval.
  - Preferred vendors have negotiated master agreements and consolidated invoicing cadence.

4) Revenue Recognition (detailed policy aligned to ASC 606 principles)
- Recognition framework (five-step model):
  1. Identify the contract(s) with a customer — must be executed, enforceable, and priced.
  2. Identify performance obligations — discrete goods/services (e.g., API access, reserved capacity seats, professional services).
  3. Determine the transaction price — fixed fees, variable consideration (usage, discounts, credits), and significant financing components.
  4. Allocate transaction price to performance obligations based on standalone selling price (SSP).
  5. Recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied.
- Typical Redwood performance obligations and treatment:
  - Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize revenue as services are delivered (consumption in the period). Monthly billed usage is accrued daily and invoiced monthly. Variable consideration: estimated refunds, credits for SLO breaches, and billing disputes are reserved.
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity commits): If contract transfers control ratably (customer access to dedicated capacity over time), recognize ratably over the commitment period. Upfront commit discounts allocated over the term.
  - Private deployments (license + services): Distinguish license (if distinct) vs. services. Perpetual licenses recognized on delivery if control transfers; time-based support and subscription components recognized over the support/subscription period.
  - Professional services and implementation: Recognize based on progress (output method — milestones completed or input method hours incurred) when measurable.
- Variable consideration and estimates:
  - Use expected value or most likely amount methodologies depending on contract portfolio.
  - Maintain an allowance for credits, estimated disputes, and refunds. Policy tolerance: reserve at least 50% of historical average dispute/credit rate for first 30 days, then roll to actuals.
- Contract modifications and renewals:
  - Treat as either a separate contract or modification per ASC 606 guidance depending on additional goods/services and price. Contract amendments > 20% of stand-alone consideration typically treated as modification requiring allocation. Legal + Finance to document modification rationale in CLM.
- Deferred revenue and journal entries (examples):
  - Invoice for annual reserved capacity commit (prepaid): Debit Cash, Credit Deferred Revenue (liability); recognize revenue monthly via Debit Deferred Revenue, Credit Revenue.
  - Usage invoice recognized when consumption occurs: Debit Accounts Receivable, Credit Revenue (if billed after usage) or record accrued revenue if billed in arrears.

  Example journal entries (simplified):
  - Prepaid annual commit of $120,000 on Jan 1:
    2026-01-01: Dr Cash 120,000; Cr Deferred Revenue 120,000
    Monthly recognition (Jan): Dr Deferred Revenue 10,000; Cr Revenue 10,000

5) Billing, Invoicing and Collections
- Billing cadence:
  - Usage-hosted: invoiced monthly in arrears by default.
  - Reserved capacity commits: invoiced per contract (monthly or annual prepaid) per SOW.
  - Private deployments and professional services: invoiced per milestones as defined in SOW.
- Payment terms and processing:
  - Standard terms: Net 30 from invoice date unless otherwise negotiated. Payment methods: ACH, wire, credit card (for self-serve), and marketplace settlement processes.
  - Late payment handling: Automated dunning sequence at 7, 21, and 35 days past due; account flagging at 45 days and escalation to collections.
- Billing accuracy and SLOs:
  - Billing accuracy target: 99.5% invoice accuracy across all customer invoices (billing ops metric).
  - Dispute resolution SLA: Billing disputes to be acknowledged within 2 business days and resolution target within 10 business days.
- Credits and refunds:
  - Credits for SLO failures: automatically calculated per credit schedule in SLA exhibit and applied on next invoice or as a credit memo.
  - One-off refunds require Finance + Legal approval for amounts > $10k.

6) Controls, Audit, and Reporting
- Monthly close and revrec controls:
  - Reconcile deferred revenue and recognized revenue monthly; variance > 2% investigated and documented.
  - Maintain revenue workpapers linking contracts in CLM to recognized revenue schedules.
- Audit readiness:
  - Store signed contracts, SOWs, and amendment history in CLM; retain billing and invoice data for 7 years per record retention policy.
  - Support external audit requests with revenue schedules, journal entries, and contract mapping.
- Internal controls and segregation of duties:
  - Billing generation and revenue recognition journal entry preparation (Billing ops/Revenue Ops) separated from posting and bank reconciliation (Treasury/Accounting).

7) Exceptions and escalation
- Material deviations from standard pricing/terms (>15% discount or custom indemnity) require Sales Head + Legal + Finance signoff and must be logged in the CLM change log.
- If ASC 606 judgment calls exceed $100k annualized impact, escalate to Controller and CFO for review.

Appendices
A. Standard billing metric definitions:
- Token: unit of model input/output as defined in pricing doc.
- Embedding unit: per-embedding request as defined in rate card.
- Reserved GPU-hour: billing unit for Dedicated capacity commits.

B. Example contract exhibit (pricing schedule)
- Service: Hosted API
  - Rate: $0.0006 per token (generation), $0.0002 per token (input)
  - Billing cadence: monthly in arrears
- Service: Dedicated reserved capacity
  - Rate: $X per reserved GPU-hour (as negotiated)
  - Billing cadence: monthly/annual per contract

C. Frequently asked questions (short)
- Q: How do we treat usage credits from promotional offers?
  - A: Promotional credits are recorded as contra-revenue through a deferral schedule that aligns redemption with usage.
- Q: Who approves contract modifications that change revenue treatment?
  - A: Finance + Legal must jointly approve prior to signature; Controller to review accounting impact.

Document maintenance:
- This policy is reviewed annually in Q4 or sooner if accounting guidance or our product pricing model materially changes. Policy owner: Head of Revenue Operations (Avery Thompson).

Contact for questions: finance@redwoodinference.com
